Model: Claude Opus 4.5

Conversation link: https://claude.ai/share/3d2aa8d2-8752-494f-9c08-bf2796196027

Setup: I uploaded the HW5 starter files (layers.py, fc_net.py, notebooks) to a Claude Project and worked through the implementations in one conversation. System prompt asked for step-by-step reasoning and commented code.

Results: 12/12 one-shot correct, 0 errors, 0 hallucinations

Question 5 - Understanding Dropout (7 parts):

5a-b: Correctly solved underdetermined least squares with pseudoinverse, explained why GD converges to same minimum-norm solution

5c-d: Built expanded dropout dataset with inverted scaling, implemented dropout layer correctly

5e: Explained why large batch size smooths training (Law of Large Numbers reduces variance)

5f: Nailed the weight ratio reversal (10:1 → 1:10) and explained dropout forces equal feature contributions

5i: Correctly analyzed cheating feature experiment - without dropout network exploits shortcut, with dropout it learns real features

Question 6 - BatchNorm/Dropout/CNNs (5 parts):

batchnorm_forward: Clean implementation with running averages and proper cache storage

dropout_forward/backward: Correct inverted dropout with mask scaling

6c: Explained the inverse relationship (higher dropout → higher train loss but better val accuracy) as regularization preventing co-adaptation

6d: Described network design and systematic hyperparameter tuning procedure

Observations:

Strong on both implementation and conceptual explanation

Unprompted connections to theory (ensemble interpretation of dropout, co-adaptation)

Code was well-commented with shape annotations throughout

No hand-holding needed - gave complete working implementations from function signatures alone
